sprint_note: Sprint01: three frontend-only UX fixes — fixed-position dropdown overflow, rep-progress chip on exercise rows, and chronologically-correct liveRow insertion in ExerciseView chart.
summary: WorkoutTracker is a session-based workout logging application that lets users record exercises with sets/reps/weight, view per-exercise history charts, and track rep-progress trends across sessions.

classification.why_application: WorkoutTracker owns domain objects (sessions, exercises, sets), enforces workout-domain rules (rep counting, history aggregation), and renders domain-specific UI flows that have no generic reuse value.
non_goals: No new backend endpoints this sprint
No changes to backend routers or database layer
No performance analytics (PerformanceView is a placeholder)
No full history view (HistoryView is a placeholder)
classification.not_platform: All logic is specific to the workout domain — session structure, exercise rep history, and per-exercise progress semantics cannot be generalized into reusable platform infrastructure.

consumes: GET /workout/sessions/{id}/exercises — Dataset of exercises for a session
GET /workout/exercises/history?name= — HistoryData (rows of past exercise entries)
provides: Read-only rep-progress delta chip on each ExerciseRow (computed client-side from historyByExercise)
Fixed-position dropdown menus in ExerciseList and SessionList (unclipped by overflow:hidden ancestors)
ExerciseView history chart with liveRow inserted at chronologically correct position
invariants: The rep-progress chip is derived entirely from already-loaded historyByExercise — no additional API calls
Dropdown position is computed from getBoundingClientRect() at open time and uses position:fixed — not relative to any ancestor
liveRow workout_date in ExerciseView equals row.workout_date (not the string 'Today')
liveRow is inserted at the correct sorted index in the history array, not always appended
failure_modes: historyByExercise entry absent for an exercise: chip renders grey with '—' (no previous data)
getBoundingClientRect() returns zero-rect if button is not mounted: dropdown renders at 0,0 — acceptable edge case on unmount

consumes: Dataset, Row, ApiError, FormField types from @platform-ui/api/types
provides: ShellEntry default export — consumed by Atlas Shell via AppRegistry

exposed_surfaces.name: ShellEntry
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Default React export consumed by Atlas Shell AppRegistry for the /workout route subtree
exposed_surfaces.ui_contract: none — this is a UI entry point, not a data endpoint

internal_flow.name: dropdown_fixed_position
internal_flow.description: In ExerciseRow, add a buttonRef (useRef) to the three-dots button. On toggle, store buttonRef.current.getBoundingClientRect() coordinates in state as buttonRect. Render the dropdown with position:fixed, top = buttonRect.bottom + 4, right = window.innerWidth - buttonRect.right. Apply the same pattern to the SessionList three-dots button.
inputs: three-dots button DOM node via useRef
outputs: dropdown rendered as viewport-level fixed overlay, unclipped by overflow:hidden ancestors

internal_flow.name: rep_progress_chip
internal_flow.description: In ExerciseRow, compute prevTotalReps from historyByExercise[row.exercise as string].rows — find the last row whose id !== row.id and sum its set1_reps..set5_reps (null-safe). Compute currentTotalReps = row.total_reps (already on the Row). Derive delta = currentTotalReps - prevTotalReps. Render a colored pill between the name/weight block and the mini HistoryChart: green (var(--atlas-chart-3), white text) if delta > 0, red (var(--md-sys-color-error), var(--md-sys-color-on-error) text) if delta < 0, grey outline (var(--md-sys-color-outline-variant) border, transparent fill, var(--md-sys-color-on-surface-variant) text, '—') if delta === 0 or no prior row.
outputs: RepChip element rendered between name block and mini chart: 36–44px wide, 20px tall pill showing '+N', '−N', or '—'

internal_flow.name: live_row_chronological_insertion
internal_flow.description: In ExerciseView, replace the liveRow workout_date value from the string 'Today' to row.workout_date. After constructing filteredHistory (history rows with current row excluded), find the correct insertion index by comparing workout_date strings lexicographically (ISO 8601 strings sort correctly). Splice liveRow into the sorted position. Pass this merged array as chart data instead of appending. When completed.some(c => c) is false, still construct liveRow using stored rep values from row (unchanged behavior — liveRow is always present at the correct position).
outputs: chart data array with liveRow at correct chronological index; liveRow._active:true distinguishes it visually

internal_required.role: apiFetch, useDataset, Dataset/Row/ApiError types, CreateForm, ErrorCard

external_required.name: recharts
external_required.role: BarChart, Bar, Cell, XAxis, YAxis, Tooltip, ResponsiveContainer

forbidden: No new npm packages — all changes use existing dependencies
No backend changes — this sprint is frontend-only

persistence.ownership: private_application_state — managed by WorkoutTracker backend; not changed this sprint

application_implementer: Item 1: Add buttonRef (useRef<HTMLButtonElement>) to ExerciseRow three-dots button; store buttonRect in state on toggle; render dropdown with position:fixed using buttonRect coordinates
Item 1: Apply same fixed-position dropdown pattern to SessionList three-dots button
Item 2: Add RepChip inline component or helper in ShellEntry.tsx that accepts delta and renders the pill
Item 2: Compute prevTotalReps in ExerciseRow from historyByExercise prop (sum set1..set5_reps of last history row with id !== row.id)
Item 2: Render RepChip between the name/weight block and HistoryChart in ExerciseRow layout
Item 3: Replace liveRow workout_date: 'Today' with row.workout_date in ExerciseView
Item 3: Compute chronological insertion index for liveRow using lexicographic comparison of workout_date ISO strings; splice instead of append
test_writer: Write UI scenario: dropdown renders above the viewport fold without clipping when triggered on last row
Write UI scenario: rep-progress chip shows correct color and delta for green, red, and grey states
Write UI scenario: ExerciseView chart positions the active bar at the correct date column for a historical session
reviewer: Verify that fixed-position dropdown coordinates account for scroll offset correctly (getBoundingClientRect returns viewport-relative coords, which is correct for position:fixed — no additional scroll offset needed)
Verify that total_reps computation in RepChip is null-safe for all five set columns
Verify that liveRow insertion handles edge cases: liveRow date earlier than all history, liveRow date later than all history, empty filteredHistory

deferred_decisions: Whether to extract RepChip as a standalone file or keep it as an inline helper in ShellEntry.tsx — left to implementer judgment

risks.impact: If the list is scrolled and the dropdown is opened, the position is still correct because getBoundingClientRect() returns viewport-relative coordinates, which are the correct input for position:fixed. No impact expected.
The draft states row.total_reps is already computed by the backend. If the field is absent on old rows, the chip will show '—' (grey, no prior data path). Implementer must null-guard row.total_reps.
If filteredHistory contains multiple rows with the same workout_date as row.workout_date, liveRow will be inserted after the last matching row — this is correct per spec (sorted order).

open_questions.question: Does the backend guarantee that rows in the history endpoint response are sorted by workout_date ascending, or must the frontend sort before insertion?
